recipes.name: Golden Rum Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Grease and flour a 10-inch Bundt pan. Sprinkle chopped walnuts evenly over the bottom of the pan.
Combine cake mix and pudding mix in a large bowl. Whisk in eggs, 1/2 cup rum, 1/2 cup water, and oil until smooth and well-blended. Pour cake batter over chopped nuts in the pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into cake comes out clean, about 1 hour.

Meanwhile, make the glaze: Combine sugar, butter, and remaining 1/4 cup water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat; cook, stirring constantly, until it thickens and slightly darkens, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in remaining 1/2 cup rum.
Cool cake in pan for 10 minutes before inverting onto a serving plate. Brush glaze over top and sides of warm cake, allowing glaze to soak in. Repeat until all glaze is used.

raw_recipe.headline: Golden Rum Cake
raw_recipe.description: This rum cake is buttery and delicious, topped with walnuts, and soaked in a decadent rum glaze for a super moist, crowd-pleasing holiday dessert.

video.description: A yummy, rummy Bundt cake with a simple butter-rum glaze.

review.reviewBody:
I've used this recipe quite a number of times and have experimented with many different rums. The best is actually a combination of two different kinds. For the cake, use Bicardi Dark/Select or Myers. For the glaze, use Appleton Estates. 

If you can't find Appleton Estates, use the Bicardi or Myers, but the Appleton really makes the glaze sweeter and almost tangy - it's strong without completely overwhelming the flavour. Captain Morgan's is also good for the cake, but I wouldn't recommend it for the glaze. Both Captain and Bicardi tend to be too heavy of a flavour while in the glaze, while Myers is exceptionally weak.

Also, some other tips: MAKE SURE YOU SIFT YOUR CAKE MIX/PUDDING! They clump really easily. Also, as others have said, use the Pillsbury since it already has the pudding mix. Use milk instead of water - fat free milk works best, honestly. When you're ready to glaze, poke holes into the top of the cake with a toothpick, pour half the glaze in the pant and re-insert the cake. Poke holes into the bottom of the cake and pour the remaining glaze over it. Let it sit for an hour or two, upside down, and then flip it over onto a plate and let it sit for a few hours to a day before serving. Personally, I just leave it in the pan on the plate, as it keeps it moist and detracts people from "picking" at it!

Absolutely delicious!! I followed the recipe exactly as to ingredients. I did add one twist, which I do with all glazed bundt cakes, have for over 50 years. I use a wooden skewer to poke 30 to 40 holes in the top and all sides of the cake. I then apply the glaze liberally with a 1 inch paint brush, used only for cooking, and repeat the process about 3 times. This way, some of the glaze penetrates the cake, adding flavor and moisture. I will definetly make this again.

This was very good and super moist!! The only thing I'll do differently next time is use about half the amount of nuts as the recipe calls for.. my hubby and I both agreed that the nuts were a little too much. 
Also, there seems to be some confusion with previous reviewers over the sugar used for the glaze. The recipe (and most other rum glaze recipes) calls for GRANULATED, also known as WHITE sugar. I would not recommend using powdered sugar as a reviewer mistakenly posted was the proper sugar to use.

Used 3 oz pkg. Cook & Serve vanilla pudding, not instant and didn't add anything else to recipe.
For a sharper rum flavor in cake, mix in rum last- after other wet ingredients (water, oil, eggs) already beaten in to dry ingredients. For a weaker rum flavor in cake, mix 1/2 c. rum with the 1/2 c. water before beating in to dry ingredients. Similarly, to decrease the alcohol in the glaze, cook the 1/2 c. of rum on low heat in a separate pan while water, butter, and sugar mixture cook- then add rum as specified. Used Gosling's Black Seal rum for both the cake and glaze and really like the flavor - great dark rum that doesn't leave lingering alcohol or cough syrup like flavors/smells. Also agree with other bakers in letting cake cool in pan for about ten minutes then pouring glaze in to let soak for an hour or so. My mother is a cookbook author so I was quite happy to learn that this is an easy recipe she likes and has baked for our family :) Cake gets better every day it sits!

My grandmother cut this recipe out of the back a presentation box for a Bacardi bottle sometime in the 1960's. We had the original recipe card for years. I have been making these as Christmas presents since the 1970's. One year my wife and I made over 40 of these. Of course that was partly because our Chesapeake Bay Retriever ate all or part of seven. The original recipe uses a 1/2 C each of rum, water and oil in the cake and a 1/4 C each of rum and water in the glaze. All other ingredients are the same. It helps if you add the eggs one at a time and blend for 20 seconds or so between each egg. Then add the pudding mix and liquid ingredients. You should also beat the batter on med. high for 3 minutes after all ingredients are blended together. Another tip is to pour half the galze over the cake as soon as it comes from the oven. Ideally the cake will float itself loose from the pan. Let it cool for 7-10 minutes and then turn out. Then drizzle the rest of the glaze over the cake. I have been meaning to try making this with a yellow cake from scratch. Back in the 90's manufacturers began adding gelatin to cake mixes (hydrolyzed animal protein) to replace the moistness imparted by evil butter. I have observed that this results in a denser finished cake that tends to sag a bit as it cools. When I first started making these they would come out taller and lighter. Still tastes just as good though. We put one of these in the mail one year and it came back to us six weeks later because the address label was lost. It was a bit dry but still perfectly edible.

Delicious 
This was so yummy! I made some changes as I put it together.
Cake:
1. I buttered and sugared the pan instead of using flour.
2. I used Pecans. I also used a cake mix with pudding in it and added a package of sugar free pudding. It worked well!
3. Included 1 teaspoon Watkins Baking Vanilla and 1 teaspoon butter Flavoring in the cake.
4. I accidentally added the softened 1/2 cup of butter to the cake. It turned out great!
5. I used Captain Morgan's Rum for the cake and glaze and it was delicious! (It was all I had in my cupboard.)
6. I poked holes in the cake, right out of the oven, with a meat thermometer.
7. The Glaze was added immediately after coming out of oven and after poking the holes.
8. 3/4 of the Glaze was allowed to soak into the bottom of the cake. After 10 minutes I inverted it onto a cake plate and topped it with remaining Glaze.
Glaze:
1. Added 1 teaspoon Watkins Vanilla Extract and 1 teaspoon Butter Rum Flavoring.
I will make this EVERY Christmas. It's an amazing Rum Cake!!!

We gifted ourselves a gas stove and this was my first baking experience preparing this cake for Christmas. Used Captain Morgan spiced rum with the liquid ingredients and Bicardi Gold with the glalze, Kerry Gold unsalted butter instead of oil and added a bit of sour cream, buttermilk instead of water and toasted the pecans in the air fryer before adding to the Bundt pan, butterscotch pudding, inverted the cake with half the glaze in the bottom of the Bundt pan, used a meat thermometer to create holes, and I have fallen in love with a Christmas favorite I'll be having from now on.

Warning ! make sure cake mix is 15.25 oz. Some mixes are 13 oz. I think it makes a difference. I made in loaf pans for gifts. For loaves I put nuts in glaze, puncture top so glaze sinks in, and use Black Seal run always.

Love this recipe. It's quick to throw together, looks as delicious as it tastes, and can easily be modified for different occasions. This time, I added a small can of pineapple tidbits after squeezing the life out of them and then sprinkling them with a bit of dry cake mix to keep them well distributed throughout the finished cake. I also added about 1/3 cup of Baker's coconut. I used pecans instead of walnuts, and then used the saved pineapple juice in lieu of water in the butter rum sauce. I also used 1/2 cup of pineapple juice and 1/4 cup of rum in the sauce as the couple receiving the finished cake would prefer it less alcohol-ly. Once I made the recipe with chopped peaches, pecans, and used bourbon in lieu of rum. Still amazingly delicious. This recipe is definitely a keeper. Be Blessed! Be a Blessing!

Instead of brushing the cake with the Rum syrup, I remove the cooked rum cake from the bundt pan, pour half the rum syrup into the bottom of the warm bundt pan, put the rum cake back into the pan and then pour the pother half of the rum simple syrup on the top of the rum cake. This totally soaks the entire rum cake and doesnt waste a drop of the syrup.
I add 1/2 tsp cinnamon to the dry ingredients. Subtle, but really good!
Inedible. There was such a bitter run taste in both the glaze and the cake. So disappointed.
Not too bad. I did use spiced apple rum instead of just dark rum, which came out pretty good. This tastes really good with ice cream and adding the rum sauce on top of it.

I made this cake to take to a Caribbean party. I always text the host and tell them what I’m going to bring to avoid 17 people bringing the same dish 😁 he told me that’s what he usually makes for his Caribbean parties, however, if I wanted to make it it would be one less thing for him too juggle. And as always, I read the reviews before I make anything and several people suggested pecans instead of walnuts so that was my only substitution. Well, it was a huge hit everyone raved about it. I had some extra sauce that I brought along, but people said it didn’t need it. I also flipped it back into the pan and let it soak up some more of the sauce and let it sit overnight. I will be putting this into the party rotation!! super easy and I’m using my mother‘s 1971 burnt orange Bundt pan. I think it’s getting more use now than back then.🤣

I've made this lots of times...EVERYONE LOVES IT and compliments me on how delicious it is. I always use pecans vs. walnuts....I live in a small, predominantly Morman community and that cake disappears faster than a road runner running from a coyote!!
I made way 2/3 glaze and still had some left over
I Love It, everyone else Loves it with some vanilla ice cream! Fabulous!!! I will always make this Rum Cake for now on!!! Thank You
Love it
Very good recipe, but I only used about half the glaze as I didn’t want the cake too wet.
I used 1/4 cup of water and 3/4 cup of rum in the batter I also added 2 tablespoons extra rum to the glaze
